question: A healthy 31-year-old woman comes to the physician because she is trying to conceive. She is currently timing the frequency of intercourse with at-home ovulation test kits. An increase in the levels of which of the following is the best indicator that ovulation has occurred?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Ovulation occurs" -> "Luteinizing hormone (LH) surge" -> "LH is a key indicator of ovulation" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Follicle matures" -> "Estrogen levels rise" -> "Estrogen peaks before ovulation" -> "Not the best indicator of ovulation" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) is released" -> "FSH stimulates follicle growth" -> "FSH levels decrease after ovulation" -> "Not a direct indicator of ovulation" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Corpus luteum forms post-ovulation" -> "Progesterone levels increase" -> "Progesterone indicates post-ovulation phase" -> "Not the best indicator of ovulation" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) released" -> "Stimulates FSH and LH release" -> "GnRH levels do not indicate ovulation directly" -> "Not a direct indicator of ovulation" -> 65%
analysis: The best indicator that ovulation has occurred is a surge in luteinizing hormone (LH). This surge triggers the release of the egg from the ovary. While progesterone levels rise after ovulation, the immediate indicator of ovulation is the increase in LH.
